facts.title: audit finding - assurance activity of material unwanted event control at P-7110

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was medical treatment injury, with 1 person injured. The potential outcome was rated 3 against the site's consequence scale, above the 2 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels was in place but did not perform, and the learning team review classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels on P-7110, M-7110 and PT-7110 and record the assurance activity before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically replacing seals and seal support fluid. P-7110 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during start-up after maintenance while the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels was in place but did not perform. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 20 January 2026 a planned assurance activity of P-7110, M-7110 and PT-7110 at Cape Verity Export Terminal found the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels not effective.
